Two real things this round, both in `Shared/` (no new files, no pbxproj touch needed):

**`AppError.conflict`'s messaging was wrong for several codes.** It had one generic string ("Someone else already acted on this request") for every `ActionConflictCode`, but that's actively misleading for `.unauthorized` (not a race — you're just not allowed to), `.expired`, and `.withdrawn` (neither is a race either). Since DEC-tech_specs-010 makes conflicts terminal for that action — no automatic retry — the message is the *only* explanation the user gets for why nothing more happens. Added `ActionConflictCode.userFacingMessage` as an extension in my own file (didn't touch `DomainModels.swift`) with real per-code copy. Deliberately used `default:` instead of an exhaustive switch — that enum's owned by data_domain and has changed shape three times already this build; an exhaustive switch here would make any future case they add a compile break on my file, which is exactly the cross-lane fragility we've spent five rounds debugging one line at a time.

**Finished the spacing-literal audit** I left open last round. Found exactly one real violation: `RelayBoardView.swift`'s board `ScrollView` had a bare `.padding(.bottom, 72)` clearing space for the floating post-request button. Added `DS.Space.floatingButtonClearance` and swapped it in — pure token substitution, zero behavior change; didn't touch whether 72 is actually the right number or whether it's redundant with the `.safeAreaInset` already in use, since that's a layout-correctness question for primary_ui, not a literal-token question for the repair pass.
